Semi-educated guess here for not liking their tails deliberately touched:

Dogs have the typical fighting strategy of biting and pulling and it's damn effective if they get any of your limbs (considering the dog is not flea-sized).

You try to pull back your limb, you help the dog damage your limb further, you step in to fight back while the dog is occupied with one of your limbs, it just naturally steps back from the pulling action and you're back where you started.

It sucks, it throws you off-balance, it's difficult to break loose, and you can't simply just wait it off because if the fucker senses you're getting too comfortable it will shake whatever it's biting so it tears and damages further at you.

We can't really deal with it very well once caught, but dogs sort of can. They're kinda built for it. Even with one limb caught they hit three spare ones to help them find a good position to fight back. Except the tail. It's hard reach something pulling at it's tail, a pull will always force all limbs to adjust their position and a very strong tug may fuck up the dog's spine.

Dogs get along pretty well with people and often even better than they get along with other dogs, but they're not people and they don't understand us all that well. They've got strong instinctive programming to protect their tails and it's probably not going away any sooner than we instinctively learn to allow strangers to touch our throats.
